rubric:
1. Places pretraining first: self-supervised next-token prediction on raw text, with no instruction or preference labels. Then SFT: curated prompt-response demonstrations, next-token loss on the response, no reward model, used to teach format and instruction following.
2. DPO: chosen/rejected pairs and a frozen reference policy, no reward model and no RL loop. Describes it as the default offline preference method, trained like a supervised classification loss.
3. GRPO: prompts plus a way to score sampled responses (a reward model or a verifier). It samples a group of responses per prompt and uses the group's scores as the baseline, so it trains no critic. Used for on-policy updates, especially reasoning.
4. RLVR: tasks with a checkable reward (tests, an exact answer, valid structure) and an automatic verifier rather than human pairs. Often that verifier is the reward inside a GRPO or PPO loop.
5. Says when to use which: SFT to teach the format, DPO when you have preference pairs and want an offline method, GRPO or RLVR when fresh samples can be scored automatically and you can afford to sample on policy.
